title: A deadline is a sealed date or instant.
A date means before that local day ends.
An instant is accepted only for the current local day.
Allocation covers fourteen days.
Projections continue past the allocation by repeating the weekday timetable, marked as approximations.
DEC-8's severity question is replaced by the notice model, with a level of info or warning and OS delivery as a flag instead of critical, warning, and informational.
Missed takes precedence: a deliverable is missed when its slack is negative or its effective deadline has passed with work remaining, whether or not a finish could be placed.
Unscheduled covers only remaining work that cannot be placed for a reason other than deadline capacity.
Blocked is the dependency graph only: a cancelled, missing, or otherwise ineligible prerequisite makes the path blocked.
The task's own state, being in the inbox, lacking an estimate, or living in a paused, completed, or archived project, makes it unscheduled.
Since projections run past the horizon, unscheduled is rare and means either that no capacity exists at all or that the task cannot be scheduled in its own right.
Reasons are six values: deadline_protection, dependency_protection, task_priority, project_priority, earlier_deadline, and stable_order.
earlier_deadline is for an order decided by an earlier effective deadline without pressure.
stable_order is for an order decided only by creation time or identifier.
The human explanation still carries the detail.
deadline_approaching is raised while an effective deadline falls within a lead window and the closure has unfinished work, for tasks and projects alike.
The lead window is configurable and defaults to twenty-four hours.
deadline_approaching defaults to level warning with OS delivery on.
deadline_tight defaults to level warning with OS delivery off.
deadline_missed defaults to level warning with OS delivery on.
blocked_deadline_path defaults to level warning with OS delivery on.
no_timetable defaults to level warning with OS delivery off.
month_will_not_settle defaults to level warning with OS delivery off.
missing_session_end defaults to level warning with OS delivery off.
estimate_overrun defaults to level info with OS delivery off.
horizon_over_capacity defaults to level info with OS delivery off.
dependency_cycle_prevented defaults to level info with OS delivery off.
Levels mean: a warning asks something of the user, info is state worth knowing.
Each notice type's level and OS delivery are settings with defaults rather than constants.
Persistence is not configurable: whether a notice describes a live condition or a one-off is a property of its source, not a preference.
A persistent notice may be dismissed, which hides it until its condition clears.
The dismissal is not remembered, so a recurrence shows again.
Quiet hours and one-delivery-per-condition apply to the OS delivery.
The count of notice types rises from nine to ten.
The four notice settings become configuration state; ForPlanningQueries returns notices with their dismissal state.
estimate_overrun is a persistent notice at info by default rather than a warning.
Agents see notices but do not dismiss them without an explicit request.
Derived notices are recomputed projections, one-off notices are stored records, and a dismissal is stored state with a lifetime tied to its condition.
Slack and therefore risk follow the day capacities, which include the monthly reconciliation and exclude vacation and zero-length flex days.
A month in arrears raises the projected capacity before a deadline and a month ahead lowers it.
A forecast whose span crosses four weeks is labelled rough.
